# thoth_slack_approvals (Resource)

Where held actions are sent for approval in Slack, and who may approve them. Install the Thoth Slack app first: that is a browser step in Settings. Reviewers are appointed by a signed-in admin, so the provider must use `use_thothctl_session`; API keys are refused. Destroying this resource removes the reviewers and leaves the channel and the Slack connection.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "thoth" {
  tenant_id            = var.tenant_id
  use_thothctl_session = true # run `thothctl auth login` first
}
```

```terraform
resource "thoth_slack_approvals" "this" {
  channel_id      = "C0123456789"
  reviewer_emails = ["ana@acme.example", "bo@acme.example"]
}
```

Each reviewer must be a verified, active member of your organization; the plan fails naming any who
are not. A reviewer who stops being a member appears by user ID in the next plan, which removes them.
Saving uses the revision it read, so a change made at the same time elsewhere is refused rather than
overwritten.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `reviewer_emails` (Set of String) Who may approve held actions in Slack, at most 50. Each must be a verified, active member of the organization. An empty set allows no one.

### Optional

- `channel_id` (String) The Slack channel ID (such as C0123456789) held actions are posted to. Unset keeps the current channel.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Terraform resource identifier (tenant ID).
- `ready` (Boolean) Whether Slack approvals are ready: a channel and at least one reviewer who can act.
- `slack_workspace_id` (String) The connected Slack workspace.

## Import

```shell
terraform import thoth_slack_approvals.this <tenant_id>
```
